Finally, we derive formulas for distributional Dirac brackets between local shear and news, and show that they contain non-local corrections.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Andrade e Silva, Simone Speziale

item.title: Isolated Critical Points for Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications of M-theory
item.description: arXiv:2605.16484v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider Scherk-Schwarz compactifications of M-theory (toroidal compactifications with a non-trivial spin structure) in various dimensions and find isolated critical points of the potential on the moduli space. We demonstrate this by identifying the unbroken duality group and finding isolated points on the moduli spaces which are fixed by elements of the unbroken duality group. We work out concrete examples involving compactifications down to $d=8,6, 5$ and $4$ spacetime dimensions. We also conjecture a duality covariant anomaly cancellation condition for M-theory on $T^n$ orbifolded by discrete $\mathbb Z_N$ symmetries acting as phases on the charge lattice. This anomaly cancellation condition generalizes the level matching requirement for perturbative string orbifolds.
item.dc:creator: Zihni Kaan Baykara, Shi Chen, Cumrun Vafa

item.title: Coherent Entanglement between Massive Oscillators from the Quantized Gravitational Field
item.description: arXiv:2606.12901v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we investigate how entanglement between two massive quantum particles trapped in harmonic oscillator potentials is generated after they interact with propagating modes of the quantized gravitational field. Specifically, we consider only the entanglement arising from the coherent contribution of the gravitational field to investigate its causal structure. We employ the Feynman-Vernon influence functional approach, within which the contribution of the coherent gravitational field to entanglement generation can be traced to the commutation relation of the gravitational field. Our analysis shows that entanglement does not arise instantaneously after the interaction begins. Instead, there is a time delay proportional to the separation between the two particles before entanglement begins to develop. This result shows that the entanglement arising from the coherent contribution of the gravitational field exhibits a causal structure. The magnitude of the resulting entanglement is generally very small. However, when the initial quantum states of the two particles are prepared as separable squeezed states, the resulting entanglement can be enhanced, with the magnitude of the enhancement depending exponentially on the squeezing parameter.
item.dc:creator: Anom Trenggana, Freddy P. Zen

item.title: Dressed Fock Spaces in Gauge Theory and Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2606.15988v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Four-dimensional gauge and gravitational theories exhibit long-range interactions that require asymptotic particles to be dressed by clouds of soft photons and gravitons. Faddeev-Kulish dressings render scattering amplitudes infrared-finite, but the resulting multi-particle states do not factorise into tensor products of dressed one-particle states. We show that this loss of Fock-space factorisation is not fundamental, but reflects an inappropriate choice of infrared variables. The real soft divergence is reproduced by the Goldstone modes of asymptotic symmetries, while the Coulomb phase is reproduced by new zero modes of the radiative fields that we introduce here. In these variables, infrared-finite dressed multi-particle states admit the usual Fock-space factorisation into single-particle dressed states.
item.dc:creator: Sangmin Choi, Prahar Mitra

item.title: Thermal Double-Twist Data in Holography
item.description: arXiv:2606.30806v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explain how to extract thermal OPE coefficients of double-twist operators in scalar two-point functions at infinite spatial volume from suitably regularized integrals of thermal response functions in momentum space. As a specific application, we implement the proposed approach to four-dimensional holographic CFTs with an Einstein bulk action, where the finite-temperature state is captured by an AdS$_5$ black-brane geometry. In that case, the thermal response function can be computed on the gravitational side by solving numerically a radial ODE reduction of the Klein-Gordon equation. We obtain accurate values of double-twist data from this solution, completing previous holographic and bootstrap studies of thermal two-point functions. Some of the reported spin-resolved data that we compute are new.
item.dc:creator: V. Niarchos, C. Papageorgakis, A. Stratoudakis

item.title: Viscoelastic and thermal response on nuclear pasta states at finite baryon density
item.description: arXiv:2607.18463v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the viscoelastic and thermal response of non-homogeneous hadronic condensates at finite baryon density representing crystals of baryonic tubes and layers. We describe them using analytic solutions of the Skyrme model in $3+1$ dimensions as ground states for a perturbative approach. At low enough temperatures, the lowest-energy excitations are described by a free massless scalar field theory in $1+1$ dimensions. We apply the Green-Kubo formulas to such excitations to obtain the elasticity tensor and other response coefficients. The analytic results of our computations are compared with available results on the nuclear pasta phase.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\'as Grandi, Scarlett Rebolledo, Aldo Vera

item.title: On the Nucleon Effective Mass in Neutron Stars Cooling
item.description: arXiv:2607.23253v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The cooling of neutrons stars, which are composed of ultra-high-density nuclear matter, strongly depends on the equation of state because the dominant cooling sources are neutrinos produced in their interiors. Here, we investigate the cooling properties of neutron stars, focusing on effective nucleon masses, whose impacts have been recently examined in supernova explosion and proto-neutron star cooling. The uncertainties of effective masses originate from the difference in the attractive interaction of scalar meson and the definition of the Dirac and Landau masses. At first, we employ so-called Walecka models that allow these two masses to be introduced within a unified framework and evaluate the resulting cooling curves. Based on the Walecka model, we compute the emissivity of the neutrons and the direct Urca process and their cooling curves. We demonstrate that the Dirac and Landau masses affect cooling of massive neutron stars, although most previous cooling simulations do not distinguish them. We also perform cooling simulations with two realistic equation of states based on relativistic mean-field (RMF) theory, whose differences arise from properties of only effective masses among characteristic parameters. These results are broadly consistent with those obtained from the Walecka models, indicating that the treatment of effective nucleon masses may be an important source of uncertainty in neutron-star cooling.
item.dc:creator: Yuuki Sugiyama, Akira Dohi

item.title: A Toy Model for Topological Entanglement Features in 1+1D Integrable Quantum Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:2607.29234v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we investigate an entanglement measure, the R\'enyi entropy, in a 1+1D integrable quantum field theory known as the Federbush model. This is a deformation of the theory of two massive Dirac fermions by means of a bilinear term in the $U(1)$ currents that couples the two fermion species. This deformation gives rise to $S$-matrix elements which are coupling-dependent phases, distinct from -1. These non-trivial phases can be seen as encoding anyon-like statistics. From this viewpoint, the Federbush model is a toy model for topological features of entanglement in one space dimension. In this paper we show that, a standard computation based on form factors of branch point twist fields leads to the conclusion that these topological features play no role when computing most known measures of entanglement at equilibrium in the ground state. This conclusion applies also to the post-quench dynamics at first order in perturbation theory, after a small quench of the topological parameter.
item.dc:creator: Emmalise J. H. Aalbers, Olalla A. Castro-Alvaredo

item.title: The facts on quantum self-dual Einstein gravity and self-dual Yang-Mills theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.26242v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Self-dual Einstein gravity is a one-loop exact, UV and IR finite, diffeomorphism invariant, non-unitary theory of quantum gravity in four dimensions. The only generically non-zero amplitudes are the one-loop-all-plus amplitudes, and they are equal to those of pure Einstein gravity. In these notes we review SDG and SDYM pedagogically. We walk the reader through key calculations, fill in some gaps in the literature, and point out directions for future research. Topics include: derivation of the self-dual actions from the full Einstein gravity/YM actions in lightcone gauge, decoupling of ghosts, Berends-Giele currents, vanishing of tree-level-one-minus amplitudes, celestial $\Lw$ symmetry, perturbiners, double-off-shell current calculation of one-loop-all-plus SDYM and SDG amplitudes, dimension shifting, unitarity cuts, the BDPR gravity formula, one-loop color ordering, perturbative dilatation symmetry of SDG, and the covariant formulations of the self-dual theories as well as their their gauge fixing. We also review some selected results from the celestial holography program.
item.dc:creator: Noah Miller

item.title: Fortuitous ABJM Operators as Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2609.08052v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a superconformal gauge theory at a fixed loop order, BPS states can be studied in two ways --- by enumerating cohomology classes of a nilpotent supercharge or by diagonalizing the anomalous dimension matrix. The second one allows for a deeper look at how holographic theories distinguish between operators based on whether they are dual to horizonless geometries or black holes. To this end, we carry out the diagonalization in $\mathrm{U}(N)_k \times \mathrm{U}(N)_{-k}$ ABJM theory with $N$ as a formal parameter. This makes it possible to define trajectories of operators and focus on the fortuitous ones which are characterized by being BPS at only finitely many values of $N$. In contrast to $\mathcal{N} = 4$ Super Yang-Mills, where it has been numerically prohibitive to study more than one of these, ABJM gives us access to 16 such trajectories along with their descendants. We show that they take an especially simple form at large $N$ where they agree with the predictions of integrability. We also show that many of them, as with black holes, can only be dressed by certain types of gravitons and comment on how this exercise in cohomology also has implications for properties of the full operators. Finally, we show that the gap to the first non-BPS state in ABJM theory qualitatively differs from that of $\mathcal{N} = 4$ Super Yang-Mills in the expected way.
item.dc:creator: Connor Behan, Leonardo Pipolo de Gioia

item.title: Alternative Boundary Conditions in Asymptotically Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2609.10805v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes are not globally hyperbolic, so boundary conditions are generally needed for well-defined dynamics. Ishibashi and Wald (IW) determined boundary conditions yielding well-posed dynamics with conserved positive energy for scalar, electromagnetic, and linearized gravitational fields, using nonlocal potentials and individual spherical harmonic modes. In this paper, we determine which IW conditions are local in the primary fields and which are AdS-invariant. In four spacetime dimensions, the standard AdS-invariant boundary conditions set the rescaled magnetic field to zero for electromagnetism and the rescaled magnetic Weyl tensor to zero for Einstein gravity on the conformal boundary. We generalize these standard boundary conditions by setting arbitrary linear combinations of the electric and magnetic fields, or the corresponding Weyl tensors, to zero, and we conjecture that these exhaust the local, AdS-invariant, conservative boundary conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$. Boundary conditions with non-AdS-invariance and in different spacetime dimensions are also studied. The AdS-invariant conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$ extend to Yang-Mills theory and nonlinear gravity in a general Fefferman-Graham setting. We construct phase spaces for these general boundary conditions. The covariant phase spaces for general conditions are naturally associated with Lagrangians containing Pontryagin terms and, in gravity, a Gauss-Bonnet term. In gravity, except for the standard boundary condition, no nontrivial asymptotic symmetries exist and all conserved charges such as ADM mass vanish identically, as in a closed universe. Spacetimes with Killing fields including AdS then exhibit linearization instability in the sense of Fischer and Marsden and Moncrief. For nonstandard boundary conditions, the modified symplectic structure yields new expressions for the entropy formula of black holes.
item.dc:creator: Robert M. Wald, Xinkang Wang

item.title: Matter Swapping between Two Branes: Conditions for a Local Type IIB D3-D7-D3 Mechanism of Charged-Fermion Mixing via E3 Instantons
item.description: arXiv:2609.17858v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Effective infrared two-sheeted descriptions of fermion mixing between braneworlds have emerged in several distinct realizations and lead to testable matter-swapping effects, motivating low-energy searches and cosmological applications. The recurrence of the same low-energy fermion operator motivates investigating whether this structure can also arise from a D-brane mechanism. We investigate the conditions under which a local Type IIB D3$_+$-D7-D3$_-$/E3 configuration can generate perturbatively forbidden interbrane mixing. Assuming the required charged zero-mode spectrum, neutral instanton measure and non-vanishing charged disk amplitudes, we derive an E3-induced chiral mass term with scalar and pseudoscalar components. The latter reproduces the characteristic mixing structure of the two-sheeted fermion operator, while D7 Wilson transport supplies the gauge-invariant relative connection between the two brane sectors. We establish the corresponding gauge matching for transitions between stationary states at resonance. This yields a conditional matching to the two-sheeted operator within the effective field theory. A separate orbifold example checks the charged zero-mode representations and the compensating instanton charge. Whether all the required instanton ingredients coexist with two independent massive D3-D7 matter sectors at separated endpoints in a single local configuration remains open. We outline a model-building roadmap toward such a configuration and its compact phenomenological embedding. Such an embedding requires electromagnetic sequestering of the two fermion sectors and a sufficiently light non-uniform D7 gauge mode mediating a long-range relative interaction. In such a compactification, the mixing parameter $g$ would be determined by microscopic instanton data and matter-field normalization, providing a connection to low-energy constraints.
item.dc:creator: Micha\"el Sarrazin

item.title: AI for BMN Strings
item.description: arXiv:2609.39769v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: With the assistance of AI (Artificial Intelligence) tools, we revisit some mathematically well-formulated problems from our previous studies of BMN (Berenstein-Maldacena-Nastase) strings on type IIB string theory pp-wave background. These mathematical problems have important physical implications, relating to the computations of higher-genus critical superstring amplitudes, possible estimate of the cosmological constant. We make significant progress on some problems, while others remain unresolved.
item.dc:creator: Min-xin Huang

item.title: Gluons and Knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.10673v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We argue that the scattering amplitude of a single minus helicity gluon with arbitrarily many positive helicity gluons is topological. The amplitude is constant in chambers of kinematic space, its resonances are located at walls and its factorization is determined by wall-crossing. Yangian invariance dictates the amplitude to be determined by a 2d null Wilson loop that can be lifted into a positive and transverse 3d link. By reinterpreting wall-crossing and the Weinberg soft theorem as skein relations and Reidemeister moves of the subknots, we construct a state-counting description consisting of adding the `corners' of their HOMFLY-PT polynomials. Beyond the classical limit, we argue that this provides a conjectured but precise connection to topological field and string theory. The new formula is rigorously derived via a Lean-formalized dependency graph (DAG) as detailed in a companion paper, laying out the precise assumptions including Reidemeister III invariance. It is further tested exhaustively, including novel `star' kinematics where the amplitude and state count are shown to become Catalan numbers, in agreement with knot theory literature.
item.dc:creator: Alfredo Guevara

item.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
item.description: arXiv:2610.16733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.
item.dc:creator: A. Ramesh Chandra, Aaghaz Mahajan, Ainesh Sanyal, Mianqi Wang, Shubhadeep Chakraborty, Sudip Chakraborty, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Rama Govindarajan, Akshit Goyal, Jonathan J. Heckman, Yasir Iqbal, Divya Jaganathan, Saumav Kapoor, Andreas Karch, Pushkar Khandare, Sandeep Krishna, Anupam Kundu, Alok Laddha, Tongyan Lin, Swarnendu Maity, Nilmani Mathur, Shani Nadir Meynet, Alessandro Mininno, Abhijeet Mishra, Vidur Niranjan, Abhishodh Prakash, Pratik Rath, Durbar Roy, Debargha Sarkar, Srikanth Sastry, Gary Shiu, Aninda Sinha, Thomas Van Riet, Praneeth Netrapalli, Suvrat Raju

item.title: Mechanical angular momentum loss at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ from static and radiative gravitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.26822v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the loss of mechanical angular momentum $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$ of two gravitationally scattering bodies at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ using worldline quantum field theory (WQFT). The gravitational memory effect, a phenomenon of the early- and late-time behaviour of the gravitational field, leads to static contributions to $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$. We illuminate how these arise: the linear memory contributes through so-called static correlators, while the nonlinear memory vanishes at this order due to symmetry considerations. The computation of the remaining, dynamical part resembles that of the $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ impulse. We generate its integrand using a reformulation of the WQFT Feynman rules that conserves four-momentum at every vertex and plainly exhibits the classical loops. The three-loop integrals are reduced to master integrals, whose differential equations and boundary matching in the post-Newtonian limit we describe in some detail. In contrast to conservative effects at this order, only polylogarithms appear. While individual contributions to the dynamical part are divergent, these cancel in $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$. The quadratic-in-radiation part of our result reproduces earlier results, while the complete result agrees with existing post-Newtonian results.
item.dc:creator: Lara Bohnenblust, Carl Jordan Eriksen, Gustav Uhre Jakobsen, Kathrin Stoldt, Andrii Yanovets

item.title: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30234v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of R\'enyi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.
item.dc:creator: L\'eo Buisine, Horacio Casini, Leandro Martinek

item.title: Monodromy Defects of 3D Wilson-Fisher Criticality on the Fuzzy Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.31269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Monodromy line defects arise as boundaries of topological symmetry surfaces, providing a natural route to conformal defects with implications in condensed matter, gauge theories and quantum information. However, their interacting dynamics remains difficult to characterize non-perturbatively. Here we realize monodromy boundary conditions in the fuzzy-sphere regularization by threading a symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We apply this construction to the $Z_2$ twist of the 3D Ising conformal field theory (CFT), the $\pi$-twist of the 3D O(2) CFT, and three inequivalent monodromies of O(3) (centre twist, z-axis $\pi$-twist and reflection). For each defect we extract the low-lying defect spectrum together with bulk-to-defect and defect-defect operator product expansion coefficients, which characterize the operators living on the defect line, their mutual interactions, and how they couple to the critical bulk. Among the resolved low-lying defect primaries we find no relevant scalar perturbation preserving all symmetries of the corresponding defect; the relevant deformations identified break at least one preserved symmetry, providing evidence that these monodromy defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations. For the partial twists of O(3), we derive the flow of the symmetry-preserving untwisted zero-mode mass generated by the bulk interaction. Its weak-coupling runaway near four dimensions motivates a careful distinction between the microscopic absence of pinning, the free reference background, and a possible infrared defect fixed point in three dimensions. These results establish a systematic set of non-perturbative conformal data for monodromy defects beyond the Ising twist, turning the symmetry flux into a tunable knob of the fuzzy-sphere regularization for exploring the response of critical matter to distinct defects.
item.dc:creator: Yin Tang, W. Zhu

item.title: Onsager Algebras and Lattice Fermions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31653v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the exact Onsager algebra of free lattice fermions in staggered, Wilson, and overlap incarnations, working in both Hamiltonian and Euclidean formulations in four spacetime dimensions. In each case, we show that the exact lattice algebra emanates the full chiral symmetry of the low-energy theory: if there are $N$ massless Dirac fermions in the continuum, the Onsager algebra reduces to a $U(2N)$ chiral symmetry. The details of which generators are quantised or ultra-local differ between formulations. There is also a trade-off between the locality of generators and the maximum compact subgroup of the Onsager algebra.
item.dc:creator: Ioanna Kourkoulou, David Tong

item.title: Fermions Scattering Off Non-Abelian Rotors
item.description: arXiv:2610.31780v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the dynamics of $d=1+1$ chiral fermions interacting with a rotor impurity. The rotors are non-Abelian, taking values in either an $SU(N)$ group manifold, or an $SU(N)/SO(N)$ coset. At low energies, the fermions pass through the impurity, seemingly unimpeded, but trailing a topological line that is necessary for current conservation. In certain cases, these topological lines exhibit non-Abelian fusion and braiding. This can be viewed as a toy model that captures aspects of s-wave monopole-fermion scattering in $d=3+1$ dimensions.
item.dc:creator: George Koundouros, David Tong

item.title: The 't Hooft model on (A)dS$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.37667v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We solve large-$N$ two-dimensional QCD with fundamental quarks---the 't Hooft model---on rigid AdS$_2$ and dS$_2$. Their isometries preserve the null gauge $A_-=0$ and in affine coordinates the curvature enters the light-front Hamiltonian only through the special-conformal generator of the null line. The $SL(2,\mathbb{R)}$ Casimir then results in an exact meson equation: 't Hooft's equation plus a Legendre operator whose sign is determined by the curvature. On AdS$_2$ it is related to equations proposed in the context of folded/segmented strings and light-front holography. The pion is massless in the chiral limit and obeys a Gell-Mann--Oakes--Renner relation that fixes the chiral condensate, the dimensions cross over from Regge to logarithmic growth once the flux tube exceeds the curvature radius, and the flat-space integrable structure survives. We also solve the problem of a quark interacting with an antiquark placed at the boundary: beyond a critical coupling the string pulls it back to the boundary, resulting in a scattering phase. On dS$_2$ and due to the expansion of space, the mesons are unstable resonances even at $N=\infty$ and eventually dissociate. Their widths are given by Boltzmann factors at the de Sitter temperature.
item.dc:creator: Panos Betzios

item.title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
item.description: arXiv:2611.06473v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions. We compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of Ising CFT at nonzero temperature. We conjecture that the QNM TBA framework should also be applicable for describing out-of-equilibrium approach to Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).
item.dc:creator: Zoltan Bajnok, Romuald A. Janik

item.title: Accessing Continuous Monodromy Defects of the 3D Conformal Field Theory on the Fuzzy Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.08102v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Monodromy defects are line defects at the boundary of a topological symmetry surface, around which charged operators acquire a symmetry phase. They probe how a critical system responds to an inserted symmetry flux, but their universal information at strongly coupled fixed points, in particular for a continuous family of twists, remains hard to access. Here we investigate the continuous family of $U(1)$ monodromy defect with fractional twist angles embedded in the three-dimensional $O(2)$ Wilson--Fisher conformal field theory. We realize this continuous family of defects within the fuzzy-sphere framework by threading a fractional Aharonov--Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We observe charged defect operators carrying fractional transverse spins, as a characteristic signature of the imposed monodromy, and a displacement operator close to its protected dimension, supporting the conformal nature of the defect line. Crucially, we resolve no relevant symmetry-preserving scalar, and identify the charge-one defect operators as the only relevant, symmetry-breaking deformations. Assuming the particle--vortex duality, the U(1) monodromy defect maps to a Wilson line of fractional charge in the critical noncompact Abelian Higgs model, and our results then provide evidence that these Wilson lines with fractional charge are locally stable conformal lines.
item.dc:creator: Yin Tang, W. Zhu

item.title: Dressed Newton-Cartan geometry and Euclidean thermal configurations in 3D
item.description: arXiv:2611.08471v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report a new class of solutions of three-dimensional Galilean Anti-de Sitter gravity. The theory can be formulated as a topological gauge theory invariant under the doubly extended Newton-Hooke group in three dimensions. The solution can be interpreted as a dressed Newton-Cartan geometry, which is endowed with four conserved charges: energy, angular momentum, spin and rest mass. Interestingly, the magnitude of the spin turns out to be bounded from above by the rest mass. The Euclidean continuation of the solution exhibits well--defined thermal properties in terms of its gauge theoretical description. Temperature, angular velocity and other chemical potentials are obtained from suitable regularity conditions associated with the topology of a solid torus.
item.dc:creator: Luis Avil\'es, Oscar Fuentealba, Diego Hidalgo, Pablo Rodr\'iguez

item.title: Thermality from a Rindler quench
item.description: arXiv:1807.04584v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ultracold fermionic atoms in an optical lattice, with a sudden position-dependent change (a quench) in the effective dispersion relation, have been proposed by Rodr\'iguez-Laguna et al. as an analogue spacetime test of the Unruh effect. We provide new support for this analogue by analysing a massless scalar field on a $(1+1)$-dimensional continuum spacetime with a similar quench: an early time Minkowski region is joined at a constant time surface, representing the quench, to a late time static region in which left and right asymptotically Rindler domains are connected by a smooth negative curvature bridge. We show that the quench is energetically mild, and late time static observers, modelled as a derivative-coupling Unruh-DeWitt detector, see thermality, in a temperature that equals the Unruh temperature for observers in the asymptotic Rindler domains. The Unruh effect hence prevails, despite the energy injected into the field by the quench and despite the absence of a late time Killing horizon. These results strengthen the motivation to realise the experimental proposal.
item.dc:creator: Jorma Louko

item.title: The Higgs boson as a self-similar system: Tsallis form factors and the electroweak hierarchy problem
item.description: arXiv:2204.09916v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the electroweak hierarchy problem for a composite Higgs boson with a statistically self-similar internal structure. Using the spectral representation of the Higgs propagator, we show that this structure can contribute only through momentum-dependent vertex functions. In a superstatistical model of the self-similar structure, a Gamma-distributed size of the constituents turns a Gaussian vertex form factor into the $q$-exponential (Tsallis) form factor $F_q(k_E^2)=[1+(q-1)k_E^2/M^2]^{-1/(q-1)}$, where $M$ is the compositeness scale and $q-1=2/(3N)$ for an effective number $N$ of constituents. These form factors interpolate between those of nonlocal field theories ($q\to1$) and Lee--Wick-type models ($q=2$). For $1<q<2$ every one-loop contribution to the Higgs mass is finite and heavy states decouple. For the benchmarks $q=11/9$, $4/3$ and $5/3$, tuning is negligible ($\Delta\lesssim1$) for $M$ up to about $1$--$2$~TeV, and remains mild ($\Delta \leq 10$) for $M$ up to about $3$--$5$~TeV. The hierarchy problem is thus converted into the requirement of new composite dynamics near the TeV scale, testable at the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider through off-shell and high-momentum Higgs processes and searches for new states near $M$.
item.dc:creator: M. Ahmadvand

item.title: Euclidean Methods on Dirac Quantization and Gauge Representation
item.description: arXiv:2404.17786v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Geometrical interpretation on U(1) gage theory of Dirac monopole, introduced here from the line integral\cite{Brandt} form of vector potentials, shows the gauge representation be multi-valued. In this paper, we construct Euclidean form of U(1) gauge theory on Dirac monopole based on the geometrical interpretation, derive the Dirac quantization condition geometrically. Even several theoretical methods which leads to Dirac quantization $eg=l/2$ has been developed, these are only possible under the postulate that gauge representation is single-valued. Using the line integration representation of vector potential, we derived the gauge equation which satisfies under the `phase gauge transformation' ($\mathbf{A}\to\mathbf{A}'=\mathbf{A}, \ \psi\to\psi'=e^{ie\Lambda}\psi$), also showed that the Dirac quantization condition can be derived by the geometrical boundary condition on this gauge equation, without any supposing of canonical quantization condition. We finally explain geometrical meaning of constant phase of gauge and how the Dirac quantization holds single valued gauge representation.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Kiryu

item.title: Viscous Gubser flow with conserved charges to benchmark fluid simulations
item.description: arXiv:2503.20021v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present semi-analytical solutions for the evolution of both the temperature and chemical potentials for viscous Gubser flow with conserved charges. Such a solution can be especially useful in testing numerical codes intended to simulate relativistic fluids with large chemical potentials. The freeze-out hypersurface profiles for constant energy density are calculated, along with the corresponding normal vectors and presented as a new unit test for numerical codes. We also compare the influence of the equation of state on the semi-analytical solutions. We benchmark the newly developed Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) code CCAKE that includes both shear viscosity and three conserved charges. The numerical solutions are in excellent agreement with the semi-analytical solution and also are able to accurately reproduce the hypersurface at freeze-out.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Ingles, Jordi Salinas San Mart\'in, Willian Serenone, Jacquelyn Noronha-Hostler

item.title: Continuous symmetry breaking in 1D spin chains and 1+1D field theory
item.description: arXiv:2506.21540v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We argue that ground states of 1D spin chains can spontaneously break U(1) ``easy-plane'' spin rotation symmetry, via true long-range order of $(S^x, S^y)$, at the phase transition between two quasi-long-range-ordered phases. The critical point can be reached by tuning a single parameter in a Hamiltonian with the same symmetry as the XXZ model, without further fine-tuning. Equivalently, it can arise in systems of bosons with particle-hole symmetry, as a long-range-ordered transition point between two quasi-long-range-ordered superfluids. Our approach is to start with the continuum field theory of the isotropic Heisenberg ferromagnet and consider generic perturbations that respect easy-plane symmetry. We argue for a renormalization-group flow to a critical point where long-range order in $(S^x, S^y)$ is enabled by coexisting critical fluctuations of $S^z$. (We also discuss multicritical points where further parameters are tuned to zero.) These results show that it is much easier to break continuous symmetries in 1D than standard lore would suggest. The failure of standard intuition for 1D chains (based on the quantum--classical correspondence) can be attributed to Berry phases, which prevent the 1+1D system from mapping to a classical 2D spin model. The present theory also gives an example of an ordered state whose Goldstone mode is interacting even in the infra-red, rather than becoming a free field.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nahum

item.title: A model of errors in transformers
item.description: arXiv:2601.14175v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the error rate of LLMs on tasks like arithmetic that require a deterministic output, and repetitive processing of tokens drawn from a small set of alternatives. We argue that incorrect predictions arise when small errors in the attention mechanism accumulate to cross a threshold, and use this insight to derive a quantitative two-parameter relationship between the accuracy and the complexity of the task. The two parameters vary with the prompt and the model; they can be interpreted in terms of an elementary noise rate, and the number of plausible erroneous tokens that can be predicted. Our analysis is inspired by an ``effective field theory'' perspective: the LLM's many raw parameters can be reorganized into just two parameters that govern the error rate. We perform extensive empirical tests, using Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek R1, and find excellent agreement between the predicted and observed accuracy for a variety of tasks, although we also identify deviations in some cases. Our model provides an alternative to suggestions that errors made by LLMs on long repetitive tasks indicate the ``collapse of reasoning'', or an inability to express ``compositional'' functions. Finally, we show how to construct prompts to reduce the error rate.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, Seoul, South Korea. PMLR 306, 2026
item.dc:creator: Suvrat Raju, Praneeth Netrapalli

item.title: Decoupling of large-scale, adiabatic inflationary perturbations from enhanced small-scale modes at one-loop
item.description: arXiv:2601.14229v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reconsider back-reaction from large amplitude, short-scale perturbations onto a long wavelength adiabatic mode. In a loop expansion of the long-mode power spectrum, this back-reaction appears first at 1-loop. Due to the separation between the long and short scales, the separate universe method provides a simple and efficient framework for this computation. In this paper, building on our earlier work, we employ a $\delta N$ formula for the long mode, which captures the effect of short scales. We show that back-reaction at 1-loop is due to either (i) non-linearity of the $\delta N$ formula, or (ii) 1-loop corrections to the initial conditions. We argue that contributions of type (ii) cannot themselves be described within the separate universe framework, but their properties can be constrained using soft theorems and a ''multi-point propagator'' expansion. When applied to a band of enhanced short-scale perturbations that crossed the horizon during inflation, our result shows that the loop correction decouples from their detailed properties. Furthermore, the back-reaction we obtain is scale-invariant. Its magnitude is model-dependent, but is degenerate with effects from modes that were still sub-horizon at the end of inflation. In this scenario (but not necessarily in all scenarios), we conclude that the effect is not observable.
item.dc:creator: Laura Iacconi, David Mulryne, David Seery

item.title: When does a lattice higher-form symmetry flow to a topological higher-form symmetry at low energies?
item.description: arXiv:2601.20935v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the lattice version of higher-form symmetries on tensor-product Hilbert spaces. Interestingly, at low energies, these symmetries may not flow to the topological higher-form symmetries familiar from relativistic quantum field theories, but instead to non-topological higher-form symmetries. We present concrete lattice models exhibiting this phenomenon. One particular model is an $\mathbb{R}$ generalization of the Kitaev honeycomb model featuring an $\mathbb{R}$ lattice 1-form symmetry. We show that its low-energy effective field theory is a gapless, non-relativistic theory with a non-topological $\mathbb{R}$ 1-form symmetry. In both the lattice model and the effective field theory, we demonstrate that the non-topological $\mathbb{R}$ 1-form symmetry is not robust against local perturbations. In contrast, we also study various modifications of the toric code and their low-energy effective field theories to demonstrate that the compact $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice 1-form symmetry does become topological at low energies unless the Hamiltonian is fine-tuned. Along the way, we clarify the rules for constructing low-energy effective field theories in the presence of multiple superselection sectors. Finally, we argue on general grounds that non-compact higher-form symmetries (such as $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{Z}$ 1-form symmetries) in lattice systems generically remain non-topological at low energies, whereas compact higher-form symmetries (such as $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ and $U(1)$ 1-form symmetries) generically become topological.
item.dc:creator: Ruizhi Liu, Pok Man Tam, Ho Tat Lam, Liujun Zou

item.title: A Generalized Landauer's Principle for Unitarily Transformed Thermal Reservoirs
item.description: arXiv:2602.04552v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Landauer's principle, a cornerstone of quantum information and thermodynamics, appears to be violated when the thermal reservoir is replaced by a squeezed thermal state (STS), owing to the additional thermodynamic resources inherently present in the squeezed state. We introduce a formal extension of the principle to such unitarily transformed thermal states. By defining an effective Hamiltonian, we rigorously establish a generalized Landauer inequality, which naturally reduces to the standard case for an ordinary thermal reservoir as a special instance. The framework further yields a consistent definition of entropy production and a proof of its non-negativity. We illustrate its utility by studying an arbitrarily moving Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to a quantum field initially prepared in the STS. Using perturbation theory, we compute the entropy production explicitly, confirming its positivity. As a result of the symmetry breaking induced by the unitary transformation, it depends on both the proper time interval and the absolute spacetime position. Our work clarifies the apparent violation of Landauer's principle with STSs by providing a consistent information-theoretic framework. It also offers a practical tool for computing entropy production in non-equilibrium and relativistic settings, with potential implications for quantum thermal machines and information protocols.
item.dc:creator: Hao Xu

item.title: Nonperturbative Resummation of Divergent Time-Local Generators: Disentangling Non-Markovian Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2603.25512v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Perturbative van Kampen cumulant expansions of time-local generators of open quantum systems generically diverge at long times, while the reduced dynamics remains regular. We show that these divergences encode information sufficient to reconstruct an approximate nonperturbative dynamical map. Although their resummation remains divergent, disentangling the dynamics according to its van Hove limit resolves the divergence and exposes its dynamical origin: the map approaches isolated times at which it becomes noninvertible. For the weak-coupling unbiased spin--boson model, the reconstructed non-Markovian dynamics takes the disentangled form \begin{equation*} \Phi=\Phi_{\mathrm{GAD}}+\Phi_{\mathrm{NS}}+\Phi_{\mathrm{Khal}}, \end{equation*} separating generalized amplitude damping, exponentially damped nonsecular coherence mixing, and a projective, phase-selective Khalfin map. Thus, the onset of recurrent noninvertibility is the reduced-dynamical-map manifestation of the Khalfin transition from exponential to algebraic relaxation. Although the coherences acquire algebraic Khalfin tails, the distinguishability of quantum superposition states remains governed by an exponential decay law well after the Khalfin transition. Comparison with numerically exact TEMPO dynamics validates the procedure and shows that apparently complex non-Markovian dynamics can resolve into a small number of distinct, physically transparent dynamical processes.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Davidovic 2026 J. Phys. A: Math. Theor.
item.dc:creator: Dragomir Davidovic

item.title: How acausal equations emerge from causal dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2604.07031v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a causal and covariantly stable kinetic model whose spectrum at real wavenumbers $k$ reproduces any rest-frame stable dissipative dispersion relation $\omega(k)$ via suitable initialization of the microscopic degrees of freedom. Macroscopic observables can therefore obey arbitrary linear evolution equations (including forms that would be acausal if taken as fundamental), while the underlying dynamics remains causal, and all apparent propagation is encoded in the initial data. This provides an explicit counterexample to the idea that microscopic causality alone constrains the analytic form of dispersion relations at real $k$. In particular, bounds on transport coefficients based solely on the analytic structure of $\omega(k)$, such as the hydrohedron bounds, require additional assumptions about the region in the complex $k$-plane where $\omega(k)$ corresponds to physical modes.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Gavassino

item.title: The Vacuum Displacement Principle: Theoretical Framework and Local Phenomenology
item.description: arXiv:2604.21050v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a modified gravitational framework in which the standard Einstein field equations are sourced by a classical matter sector coupled to a Higgs-type scalar field $\chi$ modeling a dynamic vacuum substrate. By introducing a phenomenological covariant coupling we implement a physical displacement principle where massive baryonic matter drives the vacuum field away from its vacuum expectation value. We show that this coupling leads to a field-dependent modulation of a particle's inertial rest mass alongside a spatial fifth force, yielding localized violations of the Einstein Equivalence Principle while preserving universal free fall for fundamental point masses. In the weak-field, non-relativistic limit, this interaction manifests as a Yukawa-type correction to the Newtonian potential. We test the viability of this framework against local gravitational constraints, including planetary perihelion precession and E\"otv\"os parameter limits. Finally, we model the steady-state, non-relativistic spherical accretion of dust, demonstrating that the competing effects of vacuum-induced mass modulation and fifth-force acceleration yield distinct density and velocity profiles.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Maier

item.title: Heavy Quark Transport is Non-Gaussian Beyond Leading Log
item.description: arXiv:2604.21895v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We find that heavy quark transport beyond leading logarithm at weak coupling is intrinsically non-Gaussian: the longitudinal momentum transfer distribution has asymmetric exponential tails that are crucial for equilibration dynamics. We show this by computing the leading-order momentum transfer kernel for relativistic heavy quarks in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas, matching perturbative momentum transfer on the thermal scale to hard-thermal-loop-resummed soft physics. This is the same structure previously found in strongly coupled holographic plasmas, showing that it is not peculiar to weak or strong coupling, conformality, or supersymmetry. We therefore expect that this is a robust feature that physical quark-gluon plasma should also exhibit.
item.dc:creator: Jean F. Du Plessis, Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld

item.title: A reason why we do not observe Schr\"odinger's cats
item.description: arXiv:2605.16148v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A reason is discussed (may be not the only one) for why we do not see any superposition of macroscopic states in the real world. Under the general assumption that quantum macrostates are statistical ensembles of microstates, it is shown that any superposition of macrostates is reduced in a very short time by the unitary dynamics of the ordinary Schr\"odinger equation, deducing the Born rule without having to postulate it. In more detail, the macroscopic and microscopic degrees of freedom are decoupled in the Schr\"odinger equation, yielding an effective stochastic equation for the macroscopic variables, with the ensemble average of the microscopic amplitudes that acts as a self-generated internal white noise. The stochastic equation is shown to be a reducing It\^o equation if some general causality conditions are met, predicting a very quick collapse of any macroscopic superposition upon formation, with probabilities which satisfy the Born rule. In the context of the von Neumann measurement scheme, the relevance of the result is discussed as a simple dynamical solution of the measurement problem.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Siringo

item.title: Subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures in the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces in the quantum-computing speedup theory
item.description: arXiv:2606.03859v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The quantum-computing speedup theory considers the symmetric structures and properties of quantum systems as the fundamental Quantum-Computing-Speedup (QCS) resources which are responsible for exponentially speeding up quantum computing and simulating. At present a large and important problem is how to make use of the fundamental QCS resources to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. Here the author makes a great effort toward solving this important problem. The theoretical research work in this paper is mainly divided into the two Parts I and II. The Part I investigates mainly the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces. And the relationships are analyzed among the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, quantum simulating for the unitary time-evolutional processes, and the fundamental QCS resources which exist in the different kinds of basic quantum spaces: the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, the density operator spaces, and the Hilbert spaces. It concludes that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space must be positioned as the central place where the fundamental QCS resources are exploited to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. The Part II investigates mainly the subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures. Recognize that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space is the central place. Then those fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space (a quantum-state space) must be explicitly taken into account in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space (a linear operator space). This is an important problem. The subspace-selective unitary manipulation is able to solve this problem. It aims to harness the fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space to speed up quantum computing and simulating in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space.
item.dc:creator: Xijia Miao

item.title: Retarded Correlators of Charge Transport in a Magnetic Field
item.description: arXiv:2606.08139v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study charge transport in a magnetized relativistic plasma using kinetic theory within the relaxation-time approximation. By exactly solving the linearized Boltzmann equation in a uniform magnetic field, we obtain an analytic solution for the distribution function in terms of Bessel functions. Using this solution, we compute the full set of retarded current-current correlators and verify the Ward identities. In the hydrodynamic limit, we extract the charge diffusion modes, demonstrating that the transverse diffusion coefficient is strongly suppressed by the magnetic field, scaling as $1/B_0^2$ in the strong-field regime, while the longitudinal diffusion remains unaffected. Furthermore, we analyze the non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in the complex frequency plane, determining their kinematic thresholds and identifying the underlying wave-particle interactions as longitudinal Landau damping and transverse cyclotron damping.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Zhao, Qiuze Sun, Yi Wang, Jin Hu

item.title: Ultraviolet Structure of the Gravitational-Wave Response in a Time-Dependent Scalar Medium
item.description: arXiv:2606.16296v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the real-time linear response of gravitational waves in an FLRW background with a scalar field of general time-dependent effective mass. In the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we develop an adiabatic regularization scheme for unequal-time correlation functions and use it to extract the ultraviolet structure of the one-loop response. The leading divergence reproduces the familiar $\Box ^2h_{ij}$ structure, whereas the time-dependent background induces additional local divergences proportional to $\Box h_{ij}$, $\partial_\tau h_{ij}$, and $h_{ij}$. These are renormalized by local counterterms associated with the Weyl-squared term, a time-dependent Ricci-scalar term, a time-dependent cosmological constant, and the Ricci-scalar-squared term $R^2$. The same counterterms also remove the ultraviolet divergences of the background tadpole stress tensor and agree with the known covariant counterterm results. In a flat-background Mathieu oscillator example, replacing the adiabatic vacuum by the instantaneous vacuum leaves these counterterms unchanged but introduces an initial-surface divergence, which is absorbed into the initial data rather than the bulk counterterms.
item.dc:creator: Han Lai, Atsuhisa Ota

item.title: Non-Standard Interactions and Light Z' Bosons from CEvNS Data at CONUS+
item.description: arXiv:2606.24005v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze the first Conus+ reactor-antineutrino spectrum to constrain nonstandard neutrino interactions (NSI) with quarks and light vector $Z'$ mediators in $E_6$ and leptophilic $U(1)_{L_a-L_b}$ models. The prediction includes coherent elastic antineutrino--nucleus scattering (CEvNS) and elastic antineutrino--electron scattering (EvES), with Standard Model (SM)--mediator interference in each channel and an analytically profiled normalization uncertainty. We formulate $L_e-L_\mu$ and $L_e-L_\tau$ in a common charge convention, combining direct electron scattering with the nuclear interaction induced by photon-- $Z'$ mixing. The data remain compatible with the SM. Electronic scattering has little effect on the quark-NSI and fixed-coupling $E_6$ angular regions, but substantially strengthens the low-mass coupling limits of the $E_6$ benchmarks. The leptophilic models share a common low-mass plateau dominated by electronic scattering, while their limits separate at larger mediator masses through their different nuclear loop contributions.
item.dc:creator: Ch. M. Benavides, C. S. Mu\~noz, B. C. Canas, Eduardo Rojas

item.title: Binary black hole scattering with generic spins
item.description: arXiv:2606.24432v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study generic-spin black-hole scattering with orbital-plane precession, whose dynamics require more than one scattering angle. From numerical relativity (NR), we extract the polar scattering angle and precession of the orbital plane, the latter characterised by asymptotic Euler angles. A dictionary relating post-Minkowskian (PM) observables to scattering and Euler angles is presented, enabling the first precessing PM-NR comparisons. Our results provide a key benchmark for generic-spin resummations and provide the foundations for exploring boundary-to-bound maps in the generic case.
item.dc:creator: Adam Clark, Geraint Pratten, Patricia Schmidt

item.title: Homotopies in Batalin-Vilkovisky Formalism
item.description: arXiv:2606.30965v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We review the notion of homotopy of quantum master actions in geometric Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. Then we construct new examples of such homotopies, coming from renormalization group flow and non-infinitesimal changes of gauge fixing. Finally, we use the field redefinitions given by these homotopies to construct spans of quantum master actions with isomorphic effective actions.
item.dc:creator: Branislav Jur\v{c}o, J\'an Pulmann, Martin Zika

item.title: Statistical properties of quadrangular surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.19221v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the statistical properties of random quadrangular surfaces generated by different randomization procedures: the Gruzberg-Kl\"umper-Nuding-Sedrakyan (GKNS) construction, and two newly introduced generalizations of dynamical triangulations (DT), dynamical (DQ) and general quadrangulations (GQ). We formulate these surfaces within a unified graph-theoretic framework and establish the relationships between the elementary operations defining the different ensembles. For GKNS surfaces, we demonstrate that the construction is equivalent to two mutually constrained percolation processes and determine the associated critical point and critical exponents, revealing deviations from ordinary percolation. For DQ and GQ, we analyze the underlying Markov chains and determine the scaling of mixing and relaxation times. We further analyze all three ensembles through their degree distributions, degree correlations, distance statistics, and Hausdorff dimensions. While DQ exhibits exponentially decaying degree distributions and geometric properties similar to DT, GKNS and GQ display broad, scale-free degree distributions. Moreover, GKNS surfaces possess an asymptotic Hausdorff dimension $\Delta_H\approx 2$, whereas DQ and GQ approach $\Delta_H\approx 4$, similarly to DT. This indicates that DQ is compatible with the universal behavior of DT, while GKNS and GQ define distinct classes of random geometry, implying a different underlying measure in the space of random surfaces and a possible geometric framework for a new class of noncritical string theories.
item.dc:creator: Hrant Topchyan, Rudik Badalyan, Ara Sedrakyan

item.title: Quantum Simulation of QCD in Axial Gauge
item.description: arXiv:2608.16783v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study quantum simulation of SU(3) non-Abelian gauge theory dynamically coupled with fundamental fermions in $3+1$ dimensions by employing the lattice Hamiltonian in axial gauge under fixed boundary conditions, which avoids Gauss's law constraints. The temporal component of the gauge field is analytically solved in terms of independent field degrees of freedom and a lattice regulated Green's function. The axial gauge condition is trivially maintained in time evolution, even under Trotterization. The gauge field degrees of freedom are expressed in the local field basis and can be efficiently transformed into the canonical conjugate momentum basis by local quantum Fourier transforms. We prove the number of qubits needed for describing all states up to an energy $E$ with an accuracy $\epsilon$ on a lattice of volume $V$ at bare coupling $g$ is bounded as $16n_A V + 12n_f V$, where $n_A \approx \log_2 (\frac{64 E' V^{4/3}}{\pi^2\epsilon} + \frac{32\sqrt{2}g n_f E'^{1/2} V^{7/6}}{\sqrt{3}\pi^3\epsilon^{1/2}} ) $ is the number of qubits needed for each independent gauge field per site with a shifted energy $E'$, and $n_f$ denotes the number of fermion flavors. We then analyze a quantum algorithm for time evolution that is based on Trotterization, quantum Fourier transform, and Jordan-Wigner transformation, for which quantum circuits can be explicitly constructed under arbitrary gauge field truncation and digitization. We find the numbers of CNOT and single-qubit rotation gates scale as $O(n_A^4 V^{4/3}) + O(V^{5/3})$ and $O(n_A^4 V^{4/3})$, respectively, per Trotter step for fixed $n_f\leq 6$. Together with the bounded Trotterization error, we conclude that quantum resources needed for simulating real-time dynamics of lattice QCD scale polynomially with volume, energy, time, accuracy, and bare Hamiltonian parameters.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Yao

item.title: How much averaged null energy must an anisotropic bounce violate?
item.description: arXiv:2608.29556v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that in Einstein gravity a null-complete, non-static Bianchi I universe (homogeneous, spatially flat and anisotropic) violates the averaged null energy condition (ANEC) along every complete light ray outside at most four null directions, and along all of them if its total energy density, cosmological constant included, is ever positive. Along each complete ray the averaged null energy is at most $-J_p/(8\pi G)$, with equality whenever the integral converges, where $J_p$ is the squared expansion and shear accumulated by a thin bundle of light rays. With spatial sections $\mathbb{R}^3$ the achronal ANEC therefore leaves only Minkowski space, as for flat and open Friedmann models. Under the pointwise null energy condition, every null geodesic of a non-static Bianchi I universe is incomplete. The isotropic bounce of effective loop quantum cosmology has $J_p=1.478\,\omega_B H_{\max}$ (light frequency at the bounce times largest Hubble rate), and at the same critical density the cheapest ray of a strongly anisotropic bounce pays four to five times as much. A Casimir-supported turning point on a three-torus has a deficit of the same order, but at Hubble rates well below the Planck scale its light rays circumnavigate the torus and are not achronal, so the achronal ANEC does not apply to them.
item.dc:creator: Alan Zhang, Ye Zhou

item.title: Universal Structure of Horizon Formation in Generic Binary Black Hole Mergers
item.description: arXiv:2609.11819v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A new common apparent horizon forms during a binary black hole merger and gives rise to outer and inner branches of marginally outer trapped surfaces. We derive the local structure of these branches. This event occurs in the fully nonlinear regime, outside the standard regimes of post-Newtonian inspiral theory and perturbations of a stationary black hole, yet it admits a universal description. Without assuming symmetry, we show that the stability operator of the marginally outer trapped surface must lose invertibility at formation. Outermost stability then implies that the vanishing eigenvalue is the principal one, with a strictly positive eigenfunction. Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction yields square-root branch separation with a shared linear drift. The outer and inner common horizons lie on a smooth marginally outer trapped tube along which slice time has a local minimum at formation, and nearby later slices intersect it in outer and inner branches whose separation scales as $(t-t_*)^{1/2}$. Sufficiently smooth quasilocal scalar functionals with nonzero first variation along the principal zero mode inherit the square-root separation and a shared linear term. We test these predictions in three binary black hole simulations, including an eccentric, precessing, unequal-mass system. In all three, the worldtube geometry and quasilocal scalars follow the predicted scaling. With the next-order term included, free-exponent fits to the surface geometry and quasilocal functionals recover the square-root exponent, $1/2$, to within half a percent, and diagnostics agree on the formation time within $5\times10^{-5}M$. The correlation between horizon shear and gravitational-wave news raises the possibility that common horizon formation has a signature in a short segment of the merger waveform.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Cun Xie, Vaishak Prasad

item.title: Lyapunov-controlled thermalization: an exact real-time example
item.description: arXiv:2609.20597v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A verified Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) relation, after a drive has ceased, is not sufficient evidence to prove equilibrium. We demonstrate this in a large-$N$ large-$q$ Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) quench protocol. Although all post-quench fermion correlators are exactly thermal, a second quench back to the initial Hamiltonian reveals hidden memory of the initial state. It is encoded in correlators connecting to times before the first quench. This memory is an extensive nonequilibrium (NEQ) witness with its decay rate being the Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_L$. Thus $\lambda_L$ sets the rate at which the state becomes effectively indistinguishable from a Gibbs state. Despite being a unitary interacting many-body system, the complete NEQ real-time evolution is obtained exactly in the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, making the setup ideal for analytically studying thermalization.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Loy, Jan C. Louw

item.title: Revisiting the Frolov--Zelnikov solution for Majumdar--Papapetrou black holes
item.description: arXiv:2609.23921v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We revisit Frolov and Zelnikov's electrostatic Green function for a test charge in a multi-center Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetime, correcting its horizon-charge condition and extending the result to higher dimensions. In four dimensions, we derive the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a minimally coupled spectator Maxwell field with independently prescribed horizon potentials. The horizon flux charges obey a capacitance matrix with entries $C_{AA}=M_A+\sum_{B\ne A}M_AM_B/R_{AB}$ and $C_{AB}=-M_AM_B/R_{AB}$, where $M_A$ are center masses and $R_{AB}$ their separations. This matrix is a positive diagonal term plus a weighted graph Laplacian, yielding an exact common-mode/differential-mode decomposition of the field energy. The grounded Dirichlet Green function partitions a point charge's flux among infinity and the horizons through harmonic measures. We show that the diagonal condition imposed by Frolov and Zelnikov [Eq.~(4.14)] preserves only the total horizon charge, allowing redistribution between individual horizons. A corrected symmetric Green function preserving each horizon charge instead involves the inverse capacitance matrix. For two centers, the correction produces a finite, negative-semidefinite self-energy shift and an exact self-force difference, without additional ultraviolet subtraction. Finally, we extend the capacitance matrix, flux partition, and fixed-charge Green function to $D=n+3$ dimensions, where the graph weights contain the universal factor $\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2)$.
item.dc:creator: Jongheon Baek, Gihwan Nam

item.title: Nash Equilibrium from Quantum-Field Entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2609.33188v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Entanglement harvesting allows localized probes to extract entanglement from a quantum field, even when their interaction regions are spacelike separated. However, how the resource obtained by the probes can be operationalized remains largely open. In this work, we ask whether the harvested entanglement can influence the timing choices of observers acting as players. We construct a quantum input game for Alice and Bob, each controlling an Unruh-DeWitt detector that couples to the vacuum of a free massless scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. Each player can choose an early interaction time, a late interaction time, or exit. After joint entry, a referee sends independent question qubits, so that fixed local Bell measurements and a payment table convert the detector state into a payoff. The mean payoff is proportional to minus the expectation value of an entanglement witness and is nonpositive for every separable resource. We calculate the detector state to leading perturbative order and solve the participation game analytically. Away from payoff degeneracies, every timing equilibrium with positive payoff gives two trembling hand perfect participation equilibria, in addition to mutual exit. The total count can therefore be one, three, five, or seven. For one fixed switching function and timing menu, five selected delays give the sequence seven, three, one, seven, and one. The timing payoffs follow from the field's two-point functions, with the Hadamard and Pauli-Jordan contributions to the coherence competing against local excitation noise. The resulting equilibrium structure provides an operational setting for studying how vacuum correlations and causal propagation affect the strategic use of quantum-field entanglement.
item.dc:creator: Hao Xu

item.title: Black objects in a five-dimensional swirling spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2609.37511v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use the Ehlers symmetry of the five-dimensional Ernst equation to embed the Myers-Perry black hole and the rotating black ring in a five-dimensional swirling spacetime. We show that both solutions can be made free of conical singularities, and that the swirl modifies the balance condition of the black ring. We compute horizon areas, surface gravities and Komar charges, which satisfy a Smarr relation, and study the ergoregions.
item.dc:creator: Adriano Vigan\`o

item.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (II): $[3,-1]$ blocks, VGIT, and toric phases
item.description: arXiv:2610.03688v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study mirror symmetry for a class of generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau (gCICY) threefolds via variations of GIT. Our focus is on gCICY threefolds in $\mathbb{P}^1\times B$ with a $[3,-1]$ block, cut out by sections of $O(3)\boxtimes O_B(L)$ and $O(-1)\boxtimes O_B(L+R)$, where $B$ is a smooth projective fourfold and $2L+R=-K_B$. Auxiliary variables turn the generalized section into a relative variation of GIT, whose two phases are the gCICY threefold itself and the zero locus of a rank-3 bundle on $\mathbb{P}^2\times B$, and they are isomorphic or related by $\int_B L^4$ disjoint Atiyah flops. Over products of projective spaces, there are 18 Calabi-Yau threefold configurations with a $[3,-1]$ block. All of them except the non-Gorenstein case studied in the companion paper have toric phases with Gorenstein ambient spaces and nef partitions, so that after the variation of GIT their mirror symmetry reduces to Batyrev-Borisov duality. We analyze four examples with a $[3,-1]$ block and one outside this class in detail.
item.dc:creator: Atsushi Kanazawa

item.title: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17033v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming this limitation. In the compressed overlap region of two nearly aligned jets ($\theta_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 5^\circ$), relativistic proton populations collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ -- six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in an optically thin regime ($\tau_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary TeV-EeV neutrinos and GeV-TeV $\gamma$-rays fall within the reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.
item.dc:creator: Giorgio Galanti

item.title: Scalar fields in the background of a linear Vaidya spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2610.24909v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study, in a semiclassical, quasi-stationary approximation, the entanglement properties of massless scalar fields near the event horizon of a dynamical black hole modeled by an ingoing Vaidya metric with a linearly decaying mass. In the near-horizon limit, the geometry becomes conformally equivalent to an eternal black hole, allowing the use of modular theory to analyze vacuum entanglement. We first study the modifications to the entanglement across the bifurcation surface of such a black hole from that of an eternal one. The conformal factor accounting for the evaporation modifies the Bogoliubov transformation between global modes and modes across the bifurcate Killing horizon of the black hole, inducing a phase in the thermofield-double-like structure of the global vacuum. This phase change of the vacuum state is a consequence of the adiabatic shift of the horizon. A quantitative measure of the entanglement change due to the phase is obtained through the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. We compare the CHSH inequalities in the vacuum states for the static and the linear Vaidya black holes and find that the CHSH correlation quantity for the latter is decreased by a factor dependent on the evaporation rate. Next, we discuss the analysis of the linear Vaidya black hole formed from gravitational collapse. For this purpose we adapt an analysis by Wald for the case of the Schwarzschild black hole. The entangled global vacuum again has a thermofield double structure. However, we find, as expected, the near-horizon structure and state do not approach that of the eternal black hole. Rather, the thermal factor is modified by a factor incorporating the change in the black hole mass due to evaporation.
item.dc:creator: Arielle Schutz, Ratindranath Akhoury

item.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.35669v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A string couples to a 2-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For surface amplitudes, differential characters preserve curvature and flat phases. Ordinary fake-flat crossed-module connections with a fixed flat quotient and a reference lift lead to abelian differential cocycles with local coefficients. In three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation evaluates the 2-form field sum and gives a sum of ordinary finite-group gauge partition functions. A four-dimensional quadratic example gives a signature response that admits direct cochain evaluation although replacement by an ordinary finite-group gauge theory fails. Established bundle, operator, and module descriptions provide further comparisons for topological and index invariants and twisted-sheaf moduli. For finite-dimensional smoothly separable central crossed modules, an invertible local substitution removes a pure gauge 1-form from invariant classical actions for any adjustment, leaving an ordinary quotient connection and two tensor fields. One of these tensor fields can be separated globally from the remaining lift data after fixing the quotient connection and choosing a smooth bundle splitting. For compact or semisimple quotients, an equivariant splitting makes this separation compatible with the full gauge symmetry without changing the adjustment.
item.dc:creator: Ferreira Bastien

item.title: Covariant Wigner function and spin polarization of the Rarita-Schwinger field
item.description: arXiv:2610.37382v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the covariant Wigner function for the spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field and its relation to the spin density matrix and the mean spin polarization vector. We obtain a formula relating the covariant Wigner function to the mean spin vector for a weakly interacting field. We then calculate the mean spin vector induced by thermal vorticity, thermal shear, and spin potential at local thermal equilibrium in the Belinfante, canonical and GLW pseudo-gauges. The resulting formula can be used to predict the spin polarization of spin-$3/2$ hadrons, such as the $\Omega^-$, in heavy-ion collisions. Differences in the thermal-shear induced polarization in the canonical and Belinfante pseudo-gauges make it possible to use local spin polarization measurements of the $\Omega^-$ to discriminate between the two pseudo-gauges. Lastly, we obtain the axial vortical effect conductivity for the free massive spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Buzzegoli, Aleksandar Gecic, Rajeev Singh

item.title: The quantum magic of top quarks
item.description: arXiv:2611.03211v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In recent years, a growing community of researchers has been applying ideas from Quantum Information theory to high energy physics. Entanglement is one such quantity, but there are by now many others. This contribution will examine the property of ``magic" (also known as ``non-stabliserness") which, roughly speaking, measures whether quantum systems have a genuine computational advantage over their classical counterparts. We will review the origin of this concept, before describing recent applications in collider physics, including top quark production.
item.dc:creator: Chris D. White

item.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.03429v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.
item.dc:creator: Samuel S\'anchez L\'opez, Eemeli Tomberg, Juan C. Bueno S\'anchez

item.title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
item.description: arXiv:2611.04750v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.
item.dc:creator: Xiaowei Li, Deyou Chen, Chuang Yang

item.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
item.description:
arXiv:2611.06616v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups, given one named hypothesis that is a theorem of that library, so that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.05.
item.dc:creator: Fedor K. Popov, Leonardo Rastelli
